# CompactJS Static-Link Boundary Corruption

The Awtsmoos revealed a reader failure beneath every post, where correct parser truth was widened by a later guess;
Awtsmoos.com must let a finite import keep its measured shore, so one module cannot consume the next.

## Direct evidence

The private browser failed identically for ordinary Devarim and dynamic Chitas with `ReferenceError: tsmoosPrompt is not defined`. The exact served `postLogic.js?compact=true` bundle contained `const aiify = ...default;tsmoosPrompt;` and `const parseHebrew = ...default;ult;`, while checked-in source contains valid `AwtsmoosPrompt` and `AIServiceHandler` imports.

The Merkava parser was interrogated against the real `scripts/awtsmoos/api/utils.js`. Its `ImportDeclaration.start/end` ranges are exact. The semicolonless `aiify` import ends at offset 81, immediately before the next newline; the `parseHebrew` import ends at 181.

`moduleNodeTransform.js` then discards those exact ends and calls generic `findStatementEnd(source, node.start)`. On the same real source, that scanner extends the aiify import from 81 to 127, swallowing the complete following `AwtsmoosPrompt` import, and extends parseHebrew from 181 to 231, swallowing `AIServiceHandler`. Overlapping replacement descriptors then leave corrupt identifier tails in the generated bundle.

## Repair law

Static ESM link declarations already possess authoritative parser boundaries. `ImportDeclaration`, `ExportAllDeclaration`, and source/list-only `ExportNamedDeclaration` must use a validated parser `node.end`. They must never scan forward for the next semicolon. Named exports containing an actual declaration may retain the specialized declaration-boundary path, and default exports retain their existing expression/declaration logic.

If a static module-link node lacks a finite end greater than or equal to its start, CompactJS should fail explicitly with a boundary error rather than silently consuming neighboring source.

## Verification universe

1. Add a focused parser-graph fixture with consecutive semicolonless default imports and a semicolon-terminated named import.
2. Assert the compiled module executes and all imported bindings retain their values.
3. Run the complete focused CompactJS suite.
4. Fetch the real served post reader compact bundle and assert it contains the full `AwtsmoosPrompt` and `AIServiceHandler` bindings with no stray `tsmoosPrompt` or `;ult;`.
5. Re-run private Chrome ordinary Devarim and Chitas at 390px.
6. Only after ordinary reader boot is clean should Chitas-specific UI/runtime refinement resume.
